content.comment_body: Hello everyone, After being away for a while, I'm back working with [product_name]. I have a brand new [product_name] [version_no] and an older [product_name] module. I updated the module to the latest firmware version [version_no], but I'm still having trouble with username and password—no matter what I try with the password settings, it doesn't work. The module previously worked perfectly with an older [product_name] version. Hoping to find a solution here. Thanks in advance.

There's a detail regarding communication between [product_name] [version_no] and a [product_name] module. Have you enabled the correct access protocols in the settings of the [product_name]? Also, refer to the current manual for the module, along with relevant documentation on Industrial Ethernet connections.

Yes, I've enabled both required protocols, as shown in the settings (see attached). I've checked the forum for similar cases but haven't found a solution. Perhaps I need to update the firmware on the [product_name] as well?

There's a firmware update available for the [product_name] [version_no], from one version to a newer one. Check out the topic related to current [product_name] software and firmware download links. However, I suspect the main issue is with the module's configuration. Have you checked chapter 4 of the module's manual?

Yes, I've reviewed chapter 4 of the manual. My setup appears to be correct, with everything enabled as needed. Even during monitoring, I was unable to proceed and haven't attempted to write values yet. I've updated the software to the latest version and plan to update the firmware to see if it resolves the issue. As a last resort, I may reset the module to factory settings and rebuild the configuration from scratch, since I performed the update while the old settings were present. This could be the source of the problem. Thanks in advance.

Hello, Issue resolved—here's the solution: 1) Update the [product_name] to the latest firmware. 2) Back up the module configuration if you want to keep old settings. Perform a factory reset, establish monitoring, and once it's working, back up the new configuration. Compare and copy the necessary parts from the working setup to your old configuration and restore it. Everything should work after this. Thank you to [user_name] for the help and to the supportive community.

Hello everyone, I've encountered another issue—if HTTPS is enabled on the [product_name]'s server, the configuration software can't connect. The workaround is to enable only HTTP for the onboard web server. In summary: If HTTPS is enabled along with the module, the software can't connect. If HTTP and the module are both enabled, the software works. To use both HTTPS and the software, you need to disconnect the module or power it down. I'll stick with HTTP since I need remote diagnostics. If there's an official way to report these issues, I'm willing to provide documentation and packet captures.
If you want to use HTTPS with the module, a public IP address linked to the SIM card from your provider is necessary.

This setup is still on my test bench, and I'm only working with internal IPs (not cellular or public IPs). By remote, I mean accessing the system from elsewhere in the building. I'll post some screenshots from the software. I've tested with two computers in my network using different setups (direct and indirect connections). Thanks in advance.

Dear [user_name], New issue: When HTTPS is active on the [product_name], the module doesn't respond to state changes. Switching back to HTTP for now. This requires more investigation. I will try to capture packets, but since most traffic is encrypted, I may need to work with keys from the devices to analyze unencrypted traffic. Further analysis is needed.

analysis.insight_summary: The main challenge was connecting a [product_name] module to a [product_name] [version_no] device, specifically with authentication issues following a firmware and software update. The problem was resolved by updating firmware and reconfiguring the module, including a factory reset. However, a usability issue remains: enabling HTTPS on the device server prevents the configuration software from connecting when the module is active, forcing users to choose between secure (HTTPS) and functional (HTTP) connections for remote diagnostics. The interaction highlighted compatibility and guidance gaps during firmware management.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect seamless communication between updated [product_name] devices and modules, no authentication problems after updates, and the ability to use secure HTTPS connections alongside the configuration software for remote access and management.
